summary: Mount Holmes lookout cab in Yellowstone NP, WY: built 1930 or 1931, staffed until 2007, burned by lightning July 16, 2019. No source found on what remains.

facts.design: One-story 16 x 16 ft cab on a concrete foundation, rubble-stone base, frame upper story, hip roof (register)
facts.status_note: Burned to the ground after a lightning strike on July 16, 2019

access.note: Mount Holmes Trail and summit closed after the 2019 fire, to stay closed until unsafe conditions were assessed and mitigated; no later notice found

visit.trail_note: The cab burned to the ground in 2019. The trail and summit were closed in July 2019, and we found no later notice.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The National Historic Lookout Register registered the lookout in 2004, when the cab still stood. The Former Fire Lookout Sites Register registered it in 2020, after the 2019 fire. The record's note about a standing-lookouts map is explained by that timing.

notes_for_editor: Build year conflict: the two registers say 1930; the park's 2019 press release (as reported by MTPR/YPR) and firelookout.com say 1931. The story reports both and does not settle it. Elevation: the registers say 10,256 ft (3,126 m), matching the record; firelookout.com says 10,336 ft and the 1935 Pinedale Roundup says about 10,300 ft. The record's elevation_m (3126) follows the register. The park's own press release on nps.gov (news/071719.htm) returned HTTP 404 to fetch_text; the story relies on the MTPR/YPR report that quotes it. The 2004 register entry was nominated by James Muhn; the 2020 FFLOS entry has the same nominator. The Wikidata entry links a 2012 photo on Wikimedia Commons (file 48310419056) but its licence was not checked, so no photo is proposed. The record's access field is 'unknown'; the 2019 closure is the only access statement found and is dated. Per the record's conflict note, firelookout.com does not list it on its map of standing lookouts, which matches the 2019 fire.
